name: MST Prim
description: Write build_processor(hidden_dim), returning the graph-neural-network processor (a PyTorch module) that the CLRS encode-process-decode network uses to learn Prim's minimum-spanning-tree algorithm of CLRS-30. The network is trained for 800 steps on 16-node graphs; the score is the accuracy of the predicted tree predecessor pointers on the 32 out-of-distribution 64-node test graphs (higher is better).

sources.locator: dm-clrs 2.0.3 (Apache-2.0): probe specs, encoders, decoders, Triplet-GMPNN processor, losses and evaluation ported to PyTorch; README links the CLRS-30 archive
CLRS-30 v1.0.0 dataset (85,628,509 bytes, SHA-256 7743b2f1...): train, validation and test splits of every algorithm; no separate data licence stated
CLRS benchmark: algorithms, probes, OOD protocol and metric (Velickovic et al., ICML 2022)
Triplet-GMPNN processor and single-task training setup (Ibarz et al., LoG 2022)

requirements.hardware: See upstream requirements and task notes.

notes: Architecture search uses selected CLRS tasks and discovered models are evaluated on all 30 tasks. Parameter count is minimized.

limitations: No official runnable repository was verified from the paper/project sources examined.
Upstream commands and dependencies were inspected; costly training, paid APIs, and hardware experiments were not executed.
No publicly accessible, paper-linked implementation with a verified immutable revision was established.
